name: NAW Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: New Age Wrestling built its first month around a belt it never got to award. A battle royal on the opening Anarchy made Cereal the number one contender; the two-out-of-three-falls match against TraV that followed a week later is the last thing on the only copy of that show that survives, and it stops mid-fall. Five days later the fed’s own title histories page still read Vacant, and the card for the following Saturday billed a match for the number one contendership all over again.
notes: Named on the fed’s own title histories page of 8 April 2003 as vacant; the surviving copy of the 3 April Anarchy breaks off during the match that was to fill it.

name: NAW Pacific Lightweight Championship
epitaph: The Pacific Lightweight Championship was billed for the fed’s second Anarchy — Destiny against Krissi in a Cat Fight in a Cell — and the match never happened: Destiny couldn’t reach Detroit and Krissi was attacked backstage before the bell. It stood vacant on the fed’s own title histories page five days later. Nothing else about it survives.

name: NAW Rising Star Championship
epitaph: The Rising Star Championship was the first belt New Age Wrestling actually awarded. Mystic J — billed at seven feet ten and 410 pounds, with a finisher called The 747 — beat Weaponary for it on 3 April 2003 and walked out to a backstage interview with the belt over his shoulder, the fed’s own ring announcer handing it to him in the ring first.

name: NAW Xtreme Championship
epitaph: The Redeemer became the first Xtreme Champion on 3 April 2003, a half-inch away from losing it to Xtra Ordinary by the commentary team’s own account. The card the fed posted for 12 April billed a rematch against Phil, and there the record stops — no results page for that date survives, and the card’s own stipulation labels don’t resolve cleanly enough to say under what rules.

name: NAW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The Hitmen — Renegade and Nightmare — are the only Tag Team Champions New Age Wrestling ever names. They were billed as champions defending against Lightning and Satan’s Wrath on 3 April 2003, and the surviving copy of that show carries the announcement of the match and no result for it.
